function: Predicts next-slot BS transmit and sensing beamformers, receive filter and IRS phase shifts from historical CSI, maximizing sum secrecy rate under a sensing-SNR constraint (pp. 2, 7-8).
system: IRS-enabled secure ISAC downlink: BS 64-antenna ULA, 2 single-antenna users, mobile aerial eavesdropping target, passive reflecting IRS with 50 elements, 30 GHz (Table III, p. 7; pp. 2-3).
method: DL-Net: four parallel-CNN SFE blocks, two LSTM layers, attention and fully connected layers; unsupervised offline training with penalty-based secrecy-rate loss, no labels (pp. 2, 6-8).
data_channel: Custom Rician-fading simulator (5 dB factor, path-loss exponents 2.2, 4, 2, LoS target); 4000 training, 500 validation, 500 test samples; no standard model or dataset (pp. 3, 7, 9).
test_conditions: Disjoint 4000/500/500 train/validation/test sets from one simulator (target spirals at 10 m/s); sweeps of transmit power, users, antennas, IRS elements, sensing SNR threshold; no unseen scenario (pp. 8-11).
baselines: Upper bound: perfect next-slot CSI with SDR (non-learned); EKF prediction with alternating optimization (non-learned); HCL-Net convolutional LSTM [25] (learned); LSTM and Transformer in loss comparison (p. 9).
metrics: Sum secrecy rate, average secrecy rate, sensing SNR, loss value, BS transmit beampattern (pp. 9-11).
complexity: Big-O complexity of SFE blocks, LSTM and attention, Eqs. (36)-(38); offline training Eq. (39) and online prediction Eq. (40) (pp. 8-9); no runtime or parameter count.
q1_support: p. 3: "follows the Rician fading" (Eq. 1; Rician factor 5 dB, Table III, p. 7). The channels are a custom Rician and path-loss simulator; no 3GPP model, ray-tracing dataset or measurement is named.
q2_support: p. 11: "investigate its robustness and adaptability under varying user distributions and imperfect CSI" is left to future work; p. 8: "T ∩ (X ∪ V) = ∅" shows the test set is held out from the same simulator. Figs. 8-11 (pp. 9-10) sweep users, antennas, IRS elements and thresholds without stating a model tested outside its training setting.
q3_support: p. 9: "Benchmark 2 (EKF): The EKF scheme is adopted to estimate the target's motion state" and "Benchmark 3 (HCL-Net): This scheme develops the historical channels based convolutional LSTM network"; p. 10: "the proposed scheme outperforms the EKF and HCL-Net significantly" in sum secrecy rate.
q4_support: p. 8: "The overall computational complexity of the proposed beamforming algorithm mainly includes two part: offline training and online prediction"; p. 9: "the complexity of the online prediction can be given as" Conline = τ(Cs + CL) + Ca, Eq. (40).
q5_support: p. 9: "The size of the training data, the validation data and the test data is 4000, 500 and 500, respectively". The data come from the authors' own simulator; the paper gives no code or data link, DOI, public dataset or measurements.
notes: Area 5 rather than 3: beamforming in an ISAC system, with a dedicated sensing signal s(t) in the transmit signal (p. 3), a receive filter and a sensing-SNR constraint (20c, p. 5); the IRS phase shifts are a second output. The secrecy objective does not trigger the function exclusion because the learned output is beams and IRS phase shifts serving sensing and communication. Footnote 2 (p. 3): 'we assume that each channel can be estimated via the learning approach [28]', so all CSI is assumed available. Tables I-III are images (pp. 6-7) and were read from the page images; Table III gives 64 BS antennas, 50 IRS elements, 30 GHz, Rician factor 5 dB. Whether LSTM and Transformer in Fig. 7 (p. 9) are compared on performance or only convergence is not needed for q3, which rests on EKF and HCL-Net.
